title: NFL Careers: 43 Current Job Openings at the National Football League Across the United States and Europe
summary: The National Football League (NFL) is inviting talented professionals to explore its current employment opportunities across football operations, marketing, communications, digital media, technology, finance, events, partnerships, human resources, and other specialized areas. With 43 jobs currently listed , these openings provide opportunities for professionals with different backgrounds and levels of expertise to pursue careers within one of the world’s most prominent sports and entertainment organizations. About the National Football League The National Football League is a global sports and entertainment organization built around professional American football. Beyond the games played on the field, the NFL operates across a wide range of disciplines, including media production, digital content, marketing, partnerships, communications, technology, finance, events, football operations, and community engagement. According to the NFL careers announcement, employment opportunities are available not only within the League itself but also across its 32 NFL teams , the League office in New York City , NFL Films in Mount Laurel, New Jersey , NFL Media in Inglewood, California , and international offices. The organization describes its employees as stewards of the game and emphasizes teamwork, innovation, responsibility, character, and the role football plays in bringing people and communities together. For professionals interested in working at the intersection of sports, entertainment, media, communications, marketing, technology, business, and digital content , the NFL s current vacancies offer a broad range of career possibilities. NFL Current Job Openings The NFL careers page currently lists 43 available positions spanning several departments and locations. The vacancies range from senior leadership positions to seasonal, part-time, coordinator, associate, and specialist roles. The following are some of the opportunities currently listed. 1. Brand and Partnership Management The Brand Partnership Management division includes roles focused on developing the NFL brand, engaging fans, managing partnerships, supporting players, and delivering marketing initiatives. Global Brand Consumer Marketing Senior Director, Creative — New York, United States This senior creative leadership position sits within Global Brand Consumer Marketing. It is particularly relevant to experienced professionals with backgrounds in creative strategy, brand development, advertising, marketing communications, and creative leadership. Marketing Science Strategy Director, Fan Engagement Marketing – International Club CRM Performance Marketing — New York, United States This role focuses on fan engagement, customer relationship management, performance marketing, and international club audiences. Professionals with experience in marketing strategy, digital marketing, customer engagement, analytics, CRM, or international marketing may find this area particularly relevant. Player Engagement – Brand Partnership Management Senior Manager, Player Engagement — New York, United States This position focuses on player engagement within the broader brand and partnership function. It may appeal to experienced professionals with backgrounds in partnerships, stakeholder engagement, brand management, sports business, or related fields. Social Influencer Marketing The NFL is also recruiting for several production and digital-content positions based in Inglewood, California . Current listings include: Seasonal Bilingual Video Editor, Global Creative Marketing Seasonal Live Content Correspondents Production Coordinator Seasonal Video Editor, Global Creative Marketing These positions are particularly relevant to professionals interested in video production, editing, social media content, live content, digital storytelling, and sports entertainment. Sponsorship Partnership Relations The NFL also has opportunities within sponsorship and partnership development, including: Manager, Global Partnerships Strategy — New York Manager, Sponsorship New Business — New York These roles are suited to professionals with relevant experience in business development, sponsorship, strategic partnerships, commercial relationships, sales, or marketing. 2. International Opportunities The NFL s career opportunities extend beyond the United States. International Licensing Seasonal FAST Video Systems Operator — Inglewood, California This role is associated with international licensing and focuses on video systems operations. NFL London / International Operations Senior Manager, Commercial Accounts (France) — Paris, France This international position demonstrates the NFL s expanding commercial and business operations outside the United States. The position is based in Paris, France , and is particularly relevant to experienced professionals with commercial account management, business development, partnership, or related experience. 3. Accounting and Finance The League Office also has opportunities in accounting and financial management. Current openings include: Coordinator, Accounting – Global Media — Inglewood, California Manager, Finance – League Corporate — New York Senior Coordinator, Finance – Global Partnerships — New York These roles provide opportunities for professionals with accounting, finance, financial analysis, budgeting, reporting, corporate finance, or partnership-finance experience. 4. Communications and Public Affairs For communication professionals, one of the notable vacancies is: Director, Communications – Flag Football — New York, United States This position falls under Communications Public Affairs at the League Office. A communications-focused position within the NFL can be particularly relevant for professionals experienced in areas such as: Corporate communications Public relations Media relations Strategic communications Content development Stakeholder communications Sports communications Public affairs Brand communications 5. Events The NFL s events function plays an important role in delivering major sporting and entertainment experiences. Current event-related positions include: Director, Event Location Strategy — New York Senior Manager, Global Event Production — New York These roles are relevant to professionals with backgrounds in event strategy, event management, production, venue planning, large-scale events, entertainment, or sports operations. Working in NFL events can involve the planning and execution of high-profile experiences associated with the League s global sporting and entertainment activities. 6. Football Operations The NFL also has positions directly connected to football development and operations. Current openings include: Director, Professional Adult Competitive Flag Football — New York Manager, Flag Football — New York These positions are especially relevant to professionals with expertise or experience in football administration, sports management, program development, competition management, or related areas. The presence of flag football-related positions also reflects the NFL s broader work around the development and growth of the sport. 7. Human Resources The League Office currently lists: Associate, HR Operations (External Agency Staff) — New York This opportunity is associated with human resources operations and may suit professionals with relevant HR administration, employee services, operations, or organizational support experience. 8. Information Technology The NFL is also hiring within technology infrastructure. Director, Stadium Network Architecture — Mount Laurel, New Jersey This senior technology role is focused on stadium network architecture and is relevant to experienced information technology and network infrastructure professionals. Candidates interested in this area would typically need substantial technical expertise and experience appropriate to a director-level position. 9. Social Responsibility The NFL s Social Responsibility division currently includes: Administrative Assistant (External Agency Staff) — New York This position offers an opportunity to contribute administrative and organizational support within an area associated with the NFL s broader social responsibility activities. 10. NFL Enterprises NFL Enterprises includes several commercial, digital, and media functions. Club Business Development Associate, Super Bowl Suite Sales Service (External Agency Staff) — New York This position focuses on sales and service associated with Super Bowl suites and is relevant to candidates interested in premium hospitality, sales, customer service, sports business, and commercial operations. Digital Media Content The NFL currently lists several positions in digital media content, including: Digital Content Associate (External Agency Staff) — Inglewood, California Part-Time Media Design Group Designer/Animator — Inglewood, California Seasonal Graphics Designer/Animator — Inglewood, California Seasonal Live Digital Media Specialist 2 — Inglewood, California Seasonal Part-Time Broadcast Audio 1 — Inglewood, California Seasonal Part-Time Lighting Director — Inglewood, California Seasonal Part-Time Utility — Inglewood, California Seasonal Part-Time V1/Shading Operator — Inglewood, California Seasonal Vertical Video Editor — Inglewood, California These vacancies make the NFL s current recruitment particularly interesting for people working in digital media, graphic design, animation, video editing, broadcast production, audio, lighting, live production, and visual content creation . For creative professionals, the availability of graphics, animation, video editing, and digital content positions could provide opportunities to apply creative and technical skills within a major international sports-media environment. 11. Digital Media Technology The NFL also has vacancies within digital media technology. Current positions include: Director, Broadcast Engineering — Inglewood, California Seasonal Ad Operations Coordinator — Inglewood, California Seasonal Customer Support Operations Coordinator — Inglewood, California Seasonal Part-Time TOC Operator — Inglewood, California Seasonal Product Operations Coordinator — Inglewood, California These positions demonstrate the extensive technical infrastructure required to deliver sports content and digital experiences to audiences. Candidates with experience in broadcasting, technology operations, advertising operations, customer support, product operations, or media technology may find opportunities that match their professional background. 12. NFL.com Mobile The NFL also has a senior product and design opportunity: VP, Product Design — Inglewood, California This leadership position is aimed at highly experienced professionals working in product management, digital product development, user experience, design, technology, and related areas. 13. Strategy and Business Intelligence Senior Manager, International Data Strategy — New York This position falls under Strategy Business Intelligence and is focused on international data and strategic business functions. The opportunity may be relevant to professionals with backgrounds in: Business strategy Data analysis Business intelligence International markets Strategic planning Market research Commercial analytics 14. NFL Films The NFL Films office in Mount Laurel, New Jersey , also has several seasonal opportunities. Current openings include: Seasonal Avid/Interplay Media Specialist Seasonal Football Operations Coordinator Seasonal Production Coordinator II Seasonal Project Coordinator Seasonal Rights Clearances Coordinator These positions can be particularly relevant to candidates interested in sports media production, film and television production, media asset management, football operations, project coordination, and rights management. The Avid/Interplay Media Specialist role, for example, is particularly relevant to professionals familiar with media production systems and workflows. Why Consider a Career With the NFL? A career with the NFL can provide exposure to a large-scale sports, entertainment, media, and business environment. The organization s current vacancies demonstrate that working for the NFL is not limited to athletes, coaches, or football specialists. The League requires professionals across a wide range of disciplines to operate its business and deliver experiences to fans. Depending on the role, employees can work in areas such as: Marketing and brand management Corporate communications Digital marketing Social media Graphic design Animation Video production Broadcast engineering Finance and accounting Human resources Information technology Events and production Football operations Partnerships and sponsorships Business development Data and strategy Product and digital design Media production Audio and lighting Content operations This makes the NFL careers portal potentially valuable for both specialized professionals and individuals looking to build careers in the broader sports and entertainment industry. Locations of Current NFL Jobs The vacancies listed in the supplied opportunity information are distributed across several locations. United States A significant number of positions are based in: New York, New York Inglewood, California Mount Laurel, New Jersey These locations correspond to different NFL business, media, League Office, and production functions. France The NFL also has an international opening in: Paris, France The international listing highlights the organization s presence and commercial activities beyond the United States. Who Should Consider Applying? Because the NFL has vacancies across many departments, the ideal candidate depends heavily on the individual position. Applicants should carefully review the specific requirements attached to each vacancy before submitting an application. Potentially relevant professional backgrounds include: Marketing and communications Digital marketing Social media management Content creation Graphic design Video editing Animation Photography and media production Broadcast production Finance and accounting Human resources Information technology Network architecture Business development Partnerships and sponsorships Event management Football and sports operations Data analysis and business intelligence Product management UX and digital design Project coordination Media rights and clearances Because the vacancies range from associate and coordinator positions to senior manager, director, and vice-president roles, applicants should select positions that correspond to their education, professional experience, technical skills, and career level. How to Apply for NFL Jobs Interested applicants should review the individual job descriptions carefully rather than applying indiscriminately to every available vacancy. A strong application should generally begin by identifying positions that closely match the candidate s professional background. Applicants should then: Review the job description carefully Examine the responsibilities, qualifications, experience requirements, location, employment type, and any technical or professional requirements. Assess your suitability Compare your education, work experience, technical abilities, and professional achievements with the requirements listed for the specific position. Prepare an updated CV or resume Highlight experience that directly relates to the position. For creative, communications, media, technology, or marketing roles, relevant portfolios or examples of previous work can also strengthen an application where requested. Customize your application Avoid submitting the same generic application for every role. Emphasize the specific skills and experiences that make you suitable for the position. Check the location and working arrangement Many of the listed positions are based in the United States, while at least one current opportunity is based in France. Candidates should confirm whether they can meet the location and employment requirements of their preferred role. Submit through the official NFL careers platform Each vacancy has its own application page, so applicants should use the relevant job listing when applying. APPLY HERE Important Note About Deadlines Deadline: No single application deadline is provided in the supplied NFL careers listing. These are ongoing job vacancies rather than a single scholarship, fellowship, grant, or competition with one common closing date. Individual vacancies may be removed, updated, or closed as recruitment progresses. Applicants are therefore encouraged to apply as soon as possible to positions that match their qualifications and to check the individual vacancy page for the latest application status. How to Find the Most Suitable NFL Vacancy With dozens of positions available, applicants can save time by filtering opportunities according to their professional interests. For example: Communications professionals can explore Communications Public Affairs. Digital marketers can examine Brand Consumer Marketing, Social Influencer Marketing, and Digital Media Content. Graphic designers and animators can look at Media Design Group, Graphics Designer/Animator, and related creative positions. Video editors can consider the Video Editor and Vertical Video Editor opportunities. Technology professionals can explore Broadcast Engineering, Stadium Network Architecture, and Digital Media Technology. Finance professionals can explore Accounting Finance. Event professionals can consider Global Event Production and Event Location Strategy. Business development professionals can explore Club Business Development and Partnerships. Data professionals can examine Strategy Business Intelligence. Media production professionals can explore NFL Films. Sports professionals can consider Football Operations and Flag Football positions. This approach can make the NFL careers portal more manageable and help applicants focus on opportunities that align with their strongest qualifications. Visit HERE to learn more NFL Careers. Final Thoughts The current NFL recruitment drive presents a broad selection of career opportunities across the sports, entertainment, media, marketing, technology, business, and corporate sectors. With 43 positions listed , the opportunities extend well beyond traditional football-related careers and include roles for creative professionals, communications specialists, marketers, technologists, finance professionals, event specialists, media producers, business strategists, and sports administrators. For professionals seeking to work within a globally recognized sports organization, the NFL can offer an opportunity to contribute to the delivery of major sporting events, digital experiences, media productions, fan engagement initiatives, commercial partnerships, and football operations. Interested candidates should carefully review the requirements of each position, ensure that their application accurately demonstrates their relevant qualifications and experience, and submit applications through the appropriate official vacancy page. Since the supplied listing does not specify one common deadline, applicants should avoid unnecessary delays and check their preferred vacancy for its current status. title: Niongoze Fellowship 2026: Leadership, Mentorship and Training Opportunity for Young Tanzanian Women
summary: Applications are officially open for the Niongoze Fellowship Class of 2026 , Doyenne Tanzania’s flagship leadership development programme for young Tanzanian women who want to strengthen their confidence, develop practical leadership skills and become part of a community of purpose-driven changemakers. The 2026 application window runs from: 1 September 2026 to 25 September 2026 The official Doyenne Tanzania website specifies that applications close on: 25 September 2026 at 23:59 East Africa Time (EAT). The Niongoze Fellowship is designed around Doyenne Tanzania’s broader mission of building a generation of qualified female leaders through leadership training, mentorship, coaching and empowerment . Doyenne describes the Fellowship as its flagship programme for equipping university students with transformative leadership skills. The programme is particularly relevant for young women who want to become more confident leaders, develop the skills needed to influence their communities, learn directly from experienced leaders and connect with other ambitious young women across Tanzania. Official website and application access: Doyenne Tanzania – Niongoze Fellowship 2026 About the Niongoze Fellowship The Niongoze Fellowship is a leadership development initiative created by Doyenne Tanzania , a Tanzanian nonprofit organization dedicated to expanding leadership opportunities for girls and young women. Doyenne describes itself as an organization committed to developing qualified female leaders through: Leadership training Mentorship Coaching Empowerment Professional and personal development Its wider vision is a community in which girls and women have equal opportunities to lead. The Niongoze Fellowship sits at the centre of that mission. Rather than focusing only on academic performance, the programme seeks to help young women understand leadership at a more personal and practical level: how they see themselves, how they work with other people, how they participate in organizations and how they create positive change in their communities. What Does “Niongoze” Mean for the Programme? The Fellowship is structured as a leadership journey rather than a one-off workshop. Historically, Doyenne has described Niongoze as an annual programme combining: Leadership training Mentoring Coaching Peer learning In-person activities Virtual activities Independent descriptions of the programme have characterized it as a year-long leadership development initiative in Tanzania, while Doyenne’s current website describes Niongoze as its flagship programme for university students. The overall objective is to help young women develop the knowledge, confidence and relationships needed to take increasingly meaningful leadership roles. Who Is the Niongoze Fellowship Designed For? For the 2026 application cycle, Doyenne’s official website asks: “Are you a young Tanzanian woman ready to grow in confidence, strengthen your leadership skills, and join a community of purpose-driven changemakers?” The current website also describes the Niongoze Fellowship as: A flagship leadership programme that equips university students with transformative skills. This makes the opportunity especially relevant to young Tanzanian women currently building their leadership experience while pursuing higher education. Potential applicants may include women involved in: Student government University associations Community organizations Volunteer initiatives Youth programmes Social-impact projects Advocacy STEM initiatives Entrepreneurship Health programmes Environmental initiatives Civil society activities Professional associations However, holding a formal leadership title should not automatically be assumed to be a requirement unless the application form explicitly says so. What Does the Fellowship Aim to Develop? Doyenne’s broader programme model emphasizes several interconnected dimensions of leadership. Historical descriptions of Niongoze highlight themes such as: Leadership Confidence Resilience Wellbeing and developing leadership understanding at: Individual level Group level Community level These areas are important because effective leadership involves more than holding a title. The Fellowship seeks to develop young women who can understand themselves, collaborate effectively and contribute meaningfully to the people and institutions around them. Personal Leadership The Fellowship has historically begun by focusing on: Leadership of self. This may involve areas such as: Self-awareness Confidence Personal values Decision-making Goal-setting Resilience Communication Understanding strengths Reflecting on personal growth Doyenne’s 2024 Fellowship page, for example, describes the first colloquium as focusing on personal leadership training . The idea is that leadership begins with understanding one’s own values, abilities and responsibilities. Group Leadership Another dimension concerns leadership within teams and organizations. Previous Niongoze programme structures have included training at the: Group level. Relevant skills can include: Communication Teamwork Collaboration Conflict management Listening Delegation Relationship-building Working across differences Collective decision-making These skills are particularly useful for university students who are already involved in clubs, associations, community initiatives or student leadership. Community Leadership The Fellowship also extends leadership beyond the individual and group level toward: Community leadership. Past programme descriptions include a dedicated community leadership component. This helps participants think about questions such as: What problems affect my community? How can young women contribute to solutions? How can leaders mobilize other people? How do we create sustainable impact? How can leadership strengthen inclusion and participation? This community orientation helps distinguish leadership development from purely personal career coaching. Confidence Development Confidence is a major theme of Doyenne’s work. Its current website presents the 2026 opportunity as a chance for young Tanzanian women to: Grow in confidence while building leadership capacity. For many emerging leaders, confidence can affect their willingness to: Speak publicly Express ideas Apply for opportunities Lead teams Challenge established practices Participate in decision-making Advocate for communities The Fellowship therefore seeks to create an environment where young women can develop both competence and the confidence to use it. Mentorship Mentorship forms another important part of Doyenne’s overall leadership model. Doyenne explains that its programmes connect girls with: Leaders Mentors Changemakers so participants can learn from people who have already travelled similar leadership paths. Mentorship can help emerging leaders understand: Career decisions Leadership challenges Professional development Personal growth Networking Navigating institutional environments For university students, having access to experienced female leaders may be particularly valuable when making decisions about postgraduate study, employment, entrepreneurship, public service or community leadership. Coaching and Leadership Development Doyenne also identifies coaching as part of its broader organizational approach. Coaching differs slightly from mentorship. Where mentorship often involves learning from someone’s experience, coaching can focus more directly on helping a participant: Clarify goals Recognize strengths Identify barriers Develop action plans Reflect on progress Improve leadership behaviors Taken together, leadership training, mentoring and coaching can provide participants with a broader development experience than a single short workshop. A Community of Young Female Leaders One of the strongest features of the Niongoze Fellowship is the opportunity to join a community of other young women interested in leadership. The current call specifically emphasizes joining a: “community of purpose-driven changemakers.” Peer networks can be valuable because participants may continue to support each other long after formal programme activities conclude. Fellows may come from different: Universities Academic disciplines Regions Leadership backgrounds Professional interests but share an interest in creating positive change. Previous Niongoze Fellows Have Come From Diverse Academic Fields The Niongoze Fellowship is not limited to a single academic discipline. The 2024 cohort profiled by Doyenne included young women studying areas such as: Political Science and Public Administration Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering Cybersecurity and Digital Forensics Electrical Engineering Medicine International Relations and Diplomacy Law Accounting and Finance Tourism Management Social Work This indicates that leadership development is intended to cut across academic and professional fields. A woman studying medicine may want to become a health leader. A law student may want to advance justice. An engineering student may want to lead in technology. A tourism student may want to champion sustainable development. The Fellowship provides a shared leadership platform across these different aspirations. Previous Fellows Have Represented Universities Across Tanzania Past Niongoze participants have come from institutions including: University of Dar es Salaam University of Dodoma Mzumbe University Hubert Kairuki Memorial University St. Augustine University of Tanzania College of African Wildlife Management Kilimanjaro Christian Medical University College Dar es Salaam Institute of Technology Dr. Salim Ahmed Salim Centre for Foreign Relations among others. The Fellowship therefore creates opportunities for networking beyond a participant’s own campus. Leadership Beyond Academic Achievement The profiles of previous Fellows also demonstrate that Doyenne looks broadly at leadership potential. Past participants have been involved in: Student government Health outreach Women’s empowerment STEM advocacy Child-rights advocacy Technology initiatives Conservation Environmental projects Community organizations Entrepreneurship Public speaking Student clubs Volunteer work This suggests that applicants should think about leadership as something broader than academic grades. Leadership can be demonstrated by: Starting an initiative Volunteering Representing students Solving a community problem Organizing a project Supporting peers Advocating for change Taking responsibility Leadership Training Through Colloquia Previous editions of the Fellowship have used a series of: Colloquia to structure leadership learning. Doyenne’s 2024 programme description identifies: A first colloquium on personal leadership A second colloquium focusing on leadership at the group level A third colloquium focusing on community leadership Graduation as the concluding stage Another description of Doyenne’s programme similarly notes an annual series of four colloquia delivered through physical and virtual formats. Applicants should note, however, that Doyenne’s current public 2026 homepage does not publish the complete 2026 schedule. Participants should therefore rely on the application materials or Doyenne directly for the final Class of 2026 timetable. In-Person and Virtual Learning Past Niongoze Fellowship programmes have combined: Physical activities Virtual activities rather than operating entirely online. This allows Fellows to benefit from face-to-face networking while also participating in learning and mentoring across geographic distances. The exact delivery format for the Class of 2026 should be confirmed through the application process because Doyenne’s current homepage does not publicly list every session format. Is There a Fellowship Fee or Stipend? The current 2026 Doyenne website does not publicly specify a stipend, cash award, travel allowance or financial benefit for selected Fellows. Older Doyenne communications have described participation in earlier cohorts as free, but applicants should not assume that every cost or financial arrangement is identical for the 2026 class unless this is confirmed in the current application materials. For publication accuracy, the Niongoze Fellowship 2026 should therefore not be advertised as a funded or fully funded fellowship unless Doyenne issues current 2026 financial details confirming this. Application Period Applications opened on: 1 September 2026 and close on: 25 September 2026. Doyenne’s official website provides the more precise closing time: 25 September 2026 at 23:59 EAT. Applicants should aim to submit before the final evening rather than waiting until the deadline. How to Apply Applications are available through the official Doyenne Tanzania website. Apply through Doyenne Tanzania The homepage currently displays the “Apply for the Class of 2026” option for the Niongoze Fellowship. Applicants should follow the official application link provided there. Contact Doyenne Tanzania The organization lists the following contact information: Email: info@doyenne.or.tz Phone: +255 757 019 087 Candidates with questions about: Eligibility Programme schedule Required documents Participation costs University status Application form issues should contact Doyenne directly if the information is not covered in the current application form. Application Information Session Doyenne also announced a Niongoze Fellowship information session and live Q A for 10 September 2026, reflecting its effort to help applicants understand the programme and application process. Applicants who missed that session should use the official website and Doyenne contact channels for any remaining questions. How to Prepare a Strong Niongoze Fellowship Application 1. Explain Why Leadership Matters to You Avoid simply writing that you “want to become a leader.” Explain: What type of leader you want to become Who you want to serve What problem you care about What change you hope to create A clear leadership purpose is more persuasive than a generic interest in professional development. 2. Show Leadership Through Action You do not necessarily need a prestigious title. Think about examples where you have: Organized people Solved a problem Supported classmates Volunteered Started a project Advocated for others Taken responsibility Helped your community Leadership potential often appears through action rather than formal titles. 3. Be Honest About What You Still Need to Learn A fellowship exists because applicants are still developing. You can explain that you want to improve areas such as: Public speaking Confidence Decision-making Team leadership Networking Resilience Strategic thinking Showing self-awareness can strengthen a leadership application. 4. Connect Your Leadership Goals to Tanzania The Fellowship is explicitly focused on developing young Tanzanian women. Explain how stronger leadership skills could help you contribute to: Your university Your professional field Your local community Tanzania more broadly 5. Demonstrate Community Orientation Doyenne’s Fellowship has historically moved from personal leadership to group and community leadership. A strong applicant should therefore think beyond individual career advancement. Consider: Who benefits if I become a stronger leader? That question can help shape a meaningful application. 6. Explain Why Niongoze Specifically Rather than applying because “it is a good opportunity,” explain why you value elements such as: Mentorship Leadership training Coaching Female leadership networks Learning from accomplished women Peer community This demonstrates that you understand the programme. Important Details at a Glance Programme: Niongoze Fellowship Class of 2026 Organization: Doyenne Tanzania Country: Tanzania Target group: Young Tanzanian women Current programme description: Flagship leadership programme for university students Focus: Leadership development Core approaches: Training, mentorship, coaching and empowerment Application opening: 1 September 2026 Application deadline: 25 September 2026 Closing time: 23:59 EAT Official website: www.doyenne.or.tz Email: info@doyenne.or.tz Phone: +255 757 019 087 Important Note on Age and Detailed Eligibility Previous external descriptions of Niongoze have characterized the broader programme as serving young women around 17–25 years old . However, Doyenne’s current 2026 public website does not publish a specific age range on the application announcement . It instead describes applicants as young Tanzanian women and describes Niongoze as a flagship programme for university students. For accuracy, applicants should therefore check the current 2026 application form before relying on a historical age threshold. Conclusion The Niongoze Fellowship 2026 is an important leadership development opportunity for young Tanzanian women who want to strengthen their confidence, develop practical leadership skills and connect with an ambitious community of female changemakers. Organized by Doyenne Tanzania , the Fellowship forms part of the organization’s mission to build a generation of qualified female leaders through training, mentorship, coaching and empowerment . The current Doyenne website identifies Niongoze as its flagship programme for university students. Previous cohorts demonstrate the interdisciplinary nature of the programme, bringing together women studying fields ranging from medicine and law to engineering, international relations, cybersecurity, accounting and tourism. Historically, the Fellowship has explored leadership at the personal, group and community levels and has combined physical and virtual learning experiences. For a young Tanzanian woman who wants to become more confident, develop her leadership identity, learn from mentors and build relationships with other emerging leaders, Niongoze offers a structured pathway for personal and community-oriented growth. Applications for the Class of 2026 opened on 1 September 2026 and close on: 25 September 2026 at 23:59 EAT. title: EU No Child Left Behind Grant 2026: Up to €1 Million for NGOs Supporting Children with Disabilities in Egypt
summary: The European Union has opened a major new call for proposals titled “No Child Left Behind: Inclusion and Protection for Children with Disabilities” , inviting eligible nonprofit organisations to develop projects that advance the rights, protection, participation and well-being of children with disabilities in Egypt. Published under reference EuropeAid/186723/DD/ACT/EG , the opportunity is designed to strengthen the environments in which children with disabilities live, learn and participate. It combines a rights-based approach to disability with practical interventions around child protection, inclusive education, community participation, family support, accessibility, social protection and institutional capacity. The EU Delegation to Egypt has confirmed that eligible NGOs are invited to apply and that the deadline is 30 September 2026 . The call has three major priority areas: Human rights and protection of children with disabilities Social inclusion and participation Family and enabling environments Applicants must address at least one of these priority areas, although proposals integrating more than one priority will be viewed particularly favourably during evaluation. Detailed call information reproduced by funding databases indicates an overall budget of approximately €3.9 million , with individual grants ranging from €650,000 to €1 million and projects generally lasting 24 to 36 months . Funding is reported to cover between 51% and 95% of eligible project costs , meaning most applicants will need to demonstrate an appropriate financing structure for the balance where the EU grant does not cover the full budget. A particularly important feature of the call is its emphasis on strengthening local organisations. At least 60% of eligible action costs is reported to be intended for financial support to third parties, such as Egyptian civil society organisations, community-based organisations and organisations of persons with disabilities. The normal maximum amount of support per third-party recipient is reported as €60,000 , unless a higher amount can be appropriately justified. The deadline for submission is: 30 September 2026 Applicants should consult the official EU Funding Tenders/EuropeAid documentation referenced by the EU Delegation to Egypt before submitting, since the full guidelines govern eligibility, partnership structure, budget rules, documentation and application procedure. View the EU Medbridge opportunity page About the No Child Left Behind Call for Proposals The programme responds to continuing gaps in the realisation of children’s rights in Egypt, particularly for children affected by overlapping disadvantages such as disability, poverty, social exclusion, geographic isolation and limited access to appropriate services. Egypt ratified the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1990 , and its 2014 Constitution affirms the state’s commitment to protecting children. National policies have subsequently sought to improve education, health and child-protection outcomes. Nevertheless, children with disabilities continue to experience barriers that can affect their ability to participate fully in family, school and community life. The call therefore moves beyond a narrow service-delivery model. Its overall objective is to contribute to the full realisation of the: Rights Dignity Well-being Participation Equality of children with disabilities in Egypt. It aims to achieve this by supporting inclusive social environments, strengthening families and communities, and improving the institutional and systemic capacity needed to deliver accessible and equitable services. Why This Funding Opportunity Matters Children with disabilities can experience disadvantages at several different levels simultaneously. These can include: Discrimination within families or communities Exclusion from schools Violence or neglect Limited access to health and social services Stigma Inaccessible public spaces Limited participation in community activities Barriers to social protection Insufficient family support Lack of opportunities to express their views The programme is therefore deliberately broad. It recognizes that inclusion cannot be achieved by concentrating only on the child as an individual. Effective disability inclusion also depends on: Parents Caregivers Schools Health workers Community organisations Religious and community leaders Government services Social-protection systems Accessible physical environments Public attitudes The call is designed to support interventions capable of working across those interconnected levels. Global Objective of the Call The programme’s global objective is to contribute to the: Full realisation of the rights, dignity and well-being of children with disabilities in Egypt. It intends to do so by: Promoting inclusive social environments Strengthening families Strengthening communities Improving institutional capacity Improving systemic capacity Expanding access to equitable services Expanding access to accessible services This makes the call relevant to organisations working in both direct service delivery and systems change. Specific Objective 1: Protecting the Rights of Children With Disabilities The first specific objective seeks to promote a: Rights-based approach to disability and child protection. The programme aims to protect children with disabilities from: Discrimination Neglect Violence Abuse while promoting equality. This framing is important because disability programmes can sometimes treat beneficiaries only as recipients of care. The EU call instead emphasizes children with disabilities as rights-holders . That approach can involve ensuring children and their families understand: Their legal rights Available services Social-protection entitlements Mechanisms for reporting abuse Available support systems It also means institutions and communities should understand their responsibility to respect and uphold those rights. Specific Objective 2: Inclusion and Participation The second objective is focused on ensuring that children with disabilities can participate meaningfully in: School Peer groups Community life It also aims to challenge: Stigma Harmful social norms Discriminatory attitudes that restrict children’s development, participation or voice. Participation should therefore not be interpreted simply as physical presence. A child may technically attend school but still be excluded from learning, friendships, recreation or decision-making. Meaningful inclusion involves enabling children to: Participate Communicate Learn Play Build friendships Develop skills Express opinions Influence decisions affecting their lives Specific Objective 3: Strengthening Families and Caregivers The third objective recognizes the critical role played by: Parents Caregivers Families Community actors in enabling children with disabilities to thrive. The programme seeks to strengthen their capacity while supporting family- and community-based environments that promote the child’s: Development Well-being Inclusion Participation This can involve practical caregiving support as well as: Counselling Training Peer support Financial resilience Links to social protection Community rehabilitation Priority Area 1: Human Rights and Protection of Children With Disabilities The first priority focuses on protecting children with disabilities from harm while ensuring equal treatment. Eligible or relevant activities may include promoting: Non-discrimination and equality within: Families Schools Communities This could potentially involve: Rights-awareness campaigns Community dialogue Training for teachers Child-protection mechanisms Referral systems Strengthening safeguarding practices The call is not limited to these examples, but proposed activities should clearly contribute to the programme objectives. Preventing Violence, Neglect, Abuse and Exploitation Projects under Priority Area 1 may work to prevent and respond to: Violence Neglect Abuse Exploitation affecting children with disabilities. The call specifically includes the promotion of: Positive parenting and non-violent discipline within families. This can be particularly important because children with disabilities may face heightened protection risks while also experiencing barriers to reporting mistreatment. Strong proposals might therefore combine: Prevention Awareness Identification Referral Response Family support rather than focusing only on awareness campaigns. Building the Capacity of Frontline Community Actors The call also highlights the importance of increasing awareness among frontline actors such as: Teachers Religious leaders Health workers Community volunteers These groups frequently interact with children and families and can play a central role in recognizing: Abuse Exclusion Service needs Protection risks Projects may therefore strengthen their ability to understand and uphold the rights of children with disabilities. Helping Families Access Integrated Service Cards Another possible intervention is helping children with disabilities and their families obtain: Integrated service cards and understand the rights and entitlements associated with them. This illustrates the practical nature of the call. A rights-based programme is not only about advocacy at national level. It can also help individual families navigate administrative systems and access benefits for which they are already eligible. Priority Area 2: Social Inclusion and Participation The second priority addresses the barriers that keep children with disabilities from fully participating in school and community life. Actions may support access to: Inclusive education Recreation Community activities School participation Projects might work directly with schools, communities, local organisations or families to create environments in which children with disabilities can participate alongside their peers. Inclusive Education Inclusive education is one of the clearest intervention areas under this priority. Programmes could potentially focus on: School accessibility Teacher capacity Inclusive teaching Peer support Participation in school life Family-school collaboration Prevention of discrimination The objective should be not only to increase attendance but to improve actual participation and educational inclusion. Addressing Stigma and Harmful Social Norms The call explicitly encourages initiatives addressing: Stigma and discriminatory social norms through: Awareness Community engagement Stigma can limit children even where formal rights exist. For example, negative assumptions may lead communities to believe that children with disabilities: Cannot learn Should remain at home Cannot participate in sport Cannot make decisions Should be treated differently from peers Projects addressing such attitudes should ideally go beyond one-directional awareness campaigns and promote sustained engagement with communities. Peer Interaction and Life Skills The programme also identifies: Peer interaction Life-skills development Self-advocacy as possible areas of action. This recognizes the importance of children developing: Confidence Communication Social relationships Independence Agency Projects may therefore directly support children with disabilities to become active participants rather than passive beneficiaries. Meaningful Participation in Decisions Children with disabilities should also have opportunities to participate in: Decisions affecting them. This may include decisions concerning: Education Services Community activities Programme design Family support The strongest projects may therefore involve children in programme planning, implementation or feedback processes in age- and disability-appropriate ways. Culture, Sport and Social Activities The call additionally identifies: Cultural activities Sports Social activities as important spaces for inclusion. These areas are sometimes overlooked in disability programming even though they are essential for: Friendship Confidence Belonging Personal development Community participation Priority Area 3: Family and Enabling Environment The third priority recognizes that children’s well-being depends heavily on the environments surrounding them. Projects can strengthen: Families Caregivers Communities Local services Social-protection connections Caregiver Training Actions may provide families with training on: Inclusive caregiving. This could include practical knowledge concerning: Supporting children’s development Communication Participation Independence Positive discipline Rights The precise content should reflect the needs of participating children and caregivers. Counselling and Peer Support Networks The call also identifies: Counselling Peer support as possible interventions. Caregivers can experience: Isolation Stress Financial pressure Limited access to information Peer groups can help families: Exchange information Share strategies Access emotional support Connect with services Advocate collectively Community-Based Support and Rehabilitation Eligible activities may include: Practical care assistance Community-rooted rehabilitation This can help ensure children receive support within their families and communities rather than becoming unnecessarily isolated from everyday community life. Improving Accessibility Another major intervention area is the: Physical and social accessibility of community spaces and services. Projects may therefore work on barriers affecting access to: Community centres Schools Health facilities Public services Recreation Social activities Accessibility should be understood broadly. It may involve: Physical design Communication Attitudes Procedures Information formats Connecting Families With Social Protection The programme specifically refers to strengthening connections with existing Egyptian social-protection schemes, including: Takaful Karama supplementary payments for households including persons with disabilities Public health insurance Other available entitlements This makes social-protection navigation an important possible component of a broader disability-inclusion project. Supporting the Economic Resilience of Caregivers The call also permits caregiver economic resilience to be addressed through activities such as: Livelihood programmes Community-based savings groups provided these are integrated into a broader intervention supporting the care and inclusion of children with disabilities. In other words, a standalone livelihood programme would not necessarily meet the programme purpose. Economic resilience should be linked clearly to improved outcomes for: Children Families Inclusion Caregiving Projects Addressing Several Priorities Are Encouraged A proposal is required to address at least: One priority area. However, integrated projects addressing more than one are considered particularly favourably. For example, a project might combine: Child-protection training Inclusive education Parent peer-support groups Social-protection access Local NGO funding Such a model could potentially address all three priority areas in an integrated way. Applicants should nevertheless avoid adding activities simply to appear comprehensive. Every activity should contribute logically to: The problem analysis Objectives Outputs Outcomes Funding Available Detailed call summaries report a total budget of: €3,900,000 for the programme. Individual grants are reported to range from: €650,000 to €1,000,000 per project. These are substantial multi-year grants. Applicants should therefore be capable of managing: Large budgets Partnerships Monitoring Reporting Sub-granting Safeguarding Compliance EU Funding Percentage The detailed call information reports that an EU grant may cover between: 51% and 95% of total eligible costs. Where the grant does not cover 100% of project costs, applicants will need to identify appropriate additional financing in accordance with the official rules. Prospective applicants should consult the official guidelines for: Co-financing rules Eligible sources Budget format Ineligible costs before finalising their financial plan. Project Duration Proposed actions are reported to run for: 24 to 36 months. This makes the programme suitable for interventions requiring enough time to: Build local partnerships Test approaches Strengthen organisations Work with communities Measure changes Institutionalize effective practices Applicants should propose a duration that matches the complexity of their intervention. At Least 60% of Eligible Costs for Financial Support to Third Parties One of the most distinctive elements of the programme is the requirement that a substantial share of funding be passed to smaller or local organisations. Detailed summaries report that at least: 60% of the total eligible costs of the action must be used for: Financial support to third parties. This means the lead applicant is not intended simply to implement a €1 million project itself. A central purpose is to strengthen and resource local actors. Who Could Receive Third-Party Support? Potential third-party recipients may include: Civil society organisations Community-based organisations Organisations of persons with disabilities Other eligible Egyptian nonprofit organisations Detailed call summaries indicate that third-party beneficiaries should be legally established in Egypt and have relevant experience working with or for: Children Children with disabilities Families Communities Maximum Third-Party Grant The normal maximum support to an individual third-party organisation is reported as: €60,000 unless a larger amount is specifically justified. Applicants should therefore think carefully about the structure of their proposed sub-granting mechanism. This may include: Selection criteria Application procedures Due diligence Capacity assessment Grant agreements Monitoring Reporting Safeguarding Technical support Who Can Apply? According to detailed call summaries, eligible lead applicants must be: Nonprofit legal persons established in: Egypt A European Union Member State A contracting party to the European Economic Area Agreement This means the programme is primarily aimed at organisations such as: NGOs Civil society organisations Eligible nonprofit institutions rather than individual applicants. Requirement for an Egyptian Partner Where the lead applicant is not established in Egypt , detailed call information indicates that it must apply with at least: One co-applicant established in Egypt. This partnership requirement reinforces the programme’s emphasis on: Local ownership Egyptian institutional capacity Contextual knowledge Sustainability International organisations should therefore avoid approaching the project as an externally designed intervention delivered in Egypt without meaningful local partnership. Can Individuals Apply? No. This is an organisational call for proposals. It is not intended for: Individual researchers Individual social workers Students Children Parents Individual consultants Individuals may participate in or benefit from funded projects, but they are not the direct grant applicants. Can For-Profit Companies Apply? The detailed eligibility information identifies lead applicants as: Nonprofit legal entities. Therefore, ordinary commercial companies should not be presented as eligible lead applicants unless the full official guidelines provide a specific exception. Geographic Scope All proposed action is intended to take place in: Egypt. This is not a multi-country Middle East or Mediterranean grant. Projects should primarily benefit children with disabilities, families and communities in Egypt. Application Reference The official EU Delegation announcement identifies the call reference as: EuropeAid/186723/DD/ACT/EG. Applicants should use this reference when searching the EU Funding Tenders/EuropeAid system. Application Deadline The official closing date is: 30 September 2026. Funding databases indicate that this stage concerns the initial concept-note/application stage of the EuropeAid process. Applicants should verify the exact submission time, platform instructions and two-stage procedure against the official call documents before submitting. How to Apply Applicants should begin by reviewing the full official call documentation referenced by the EU Delegation to Egypt. The official announcement confirms that the: Full guidelines Eligibility rules Application documents are available through the EU Funding Tenders Portal . SUBMIT HERE Applicants should search using: EuropeAid/186723/DD/ACT/EG and ensure they are working from the final official documentation rather than summaries circulated on social media. What a Strong Proposal Should Demonstrate 1. A Clear Rights-Based Approach The proposal should treat children with disabilities as: Rights-holders rather than only service recipients. Explain how the intervention will promote: Equality Agency Participation Protection Dignity 2. Genuine Participation of Children With Disabilities Applicants should consider how children themselves can help shape: Project activities Feedback systems Monitoring Decisions affecting them Participation mechanisms should be: Safe Accessible Age appropriate Disability inclusive 3. Strong Safeguarding Systems Projects involving children need robust safeguarding. Applicants should be ready to demonstrate policies and systems concerning: Child protection Reporting Referral Staff conduct Prevention of exploitation and abuse Protection of personal data 4. Meaningful Engagement With Organisations of Persons With Disabilities Disability inclusion programmes are stronger when people with disabilities and their representative organisations participate in: Design Implementation Governance Monitoring Rather than being consulted only after a project has already been developed. 5. Strong Local Partnerships Since at least 60% of eligible costs is reportedly intended for third-party support, applicants need a credible strategy for working with local organisations. Explain: Which types of organisations will be supported How they will be selected How grants will be managed What capacity support they will receive How sustainability will be strengthened 6. Integration Across the Three Priorities Projects addressing more than one priority may be viewed particularly favourably. A strong integrated intervention could connect: Protection → inclusion → family support instead of treating each problem separately. 7. Sustainability A 24–36 month grant will eventually end. Applicants should explain what remains after EU funding stops. Possible sustainability mechanisms can include: Strengthened local organisations Institutionalised procedures Trained frontline workers Parent networks Better referral mechanisms Stronger government-CSO coordination Sustainable social-protection access 8. Accessibility Accessibility should not be an afterthought. Applicants should think about: Physical accessibility Accessible communication Digital accessibility Accessible events Accessible information formats Participation accommodations Key Details at a Glance Call title: No Child Left Behind: Inclusion and Protection for Children with Disabilities Reference: EuropeAid/186723/DD/ACT/EG Funder: European Union / European Commission Country of implementation: Egypt Overall objective: Advance the rights, dignity and well-being of children with disabilities Priority 1: Human Rights and Protection Priority 2: Social Inclusion and Participation Priority 3: Family and Enabling Environment Total reported budget: €3.9 million Reported grant size: €650,000–€1 million Reported EU contribution: 51%–95% of eligible costs Reported project duration: 24–36 months Financial support to third parties: At least 60% of eligible action costs, according to detailed call summaries Normal reported maximum per third party: €60,000 unless otherwise justified Lead applicant: Nonprofit legal entity Lead applicant location: Egypt, EU Member State or EEA contracting party, according to detailed call information Egyptian co-applicant: Required where the lead applicant is not established in Egypt Application deadline: 30 September 2026 Conclusion The EU No Child Left Behind: Inclusion and Protection for Children with Disabilities call for proposals 2026 represents a substantial funding opportunity for nonprofit organisations working at the intersection of: Disability inclusion Child protection Inclusive education Human rights Family support Social protection Community development in Egypt. The call aims to move beyond isolated disability services by promoting a broader rights-based model in which children with disabilities are protected from discrimination and abuse, participate meaningfully in education and community life, and grow up in families and communities equipped to support their well-being. Three interconnected priorities structure the programme: human rights and protection, social inclusion and participation, and family and enabling environments . Proposals must address at least one, while integrated approaches addressing several priorities will be considered particularly positively. Detailed call information reports a €3.9 million overall budget , individual grants of approximately €650,000 to €1 million , implementation periods of 24 to 36 months , and EU support covering approximately 51% to 95% of eligible costs . A particularly significant component is the reported requirement to direct at least 60% of eligible project costs toward financial support to third parties , helping ensure that community organisations, local CSOs and organisations of persons with disabilities receive resources and capacity support rather than being treated solely as downstream implementing partners. Eligible lead organisations are reported to be nonprofit legal entities established in Egypt, an EU Member State or an EEA contracting country. A non-Egyptian lead applicant must work with at least one Egyptian co-applicant. All supported action is focused on Egypt. The deadline is: 30 September 2026. Organisations considering an application should review the official guidelines under reference EuropeAid/186723/DD/ACT/EG carefully before preparing a submission.
