title: University of Saskatchewan Toxicology MSc and PhD 2026–2027: Funded Graduate Study in Canada With Guaranteed Stipends
summary: The University of Saskatchewan (USask) Toxicology Graduate Program is accepting applications for its research-intensive Master of Science (M.Sc.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) programs in Toxicology in Canada. The program is particularly attractive to students interested in environmental health, contaminant science, ecological risk assessment, human health, wildlife toxicology, analytical toxicology, molecular toxicology, and related scientific fields. One of the most important features of the program is its funding structure. The University of Saskatchewan states that all graduate students accepted into the Toxicology Graduate Program are guaranteed funding , with current minimum stipends of CAD 23,000 for master s students and CAD 26,000 for doctoral students . The Toxicology Centre separately describes accepted students as receiving full funding once they have secured a research supervisor and satisfied admission requirements. Another major advantage is application flexibility. There is no fixed application deadline for the Toxicology M.Sc. or Ph.D. programs. Applications are accepted continuously throughout the year, and students may start their studies in January, May, or September . Both Canadian and international applicants can apply, subject to academic, English-language, research, and admission requirements. About the University of Saskatchewan Toxicology Graduate Program The Toxicology Graduate Program is an interdisciplinary research program at the University of Saskatchewan. It offers research-based M.Sc. and Ph.D. pathways designed to prepare students to investigate the effects of contaminants and potentially harmful physical or chemical agents on human beings, animals, ecosystems, and biological systems. Research and postgraduate education in toxicology are coordinated through the University of Saskatchewan Toxicology Centre and involve academics from numerous university departments as well as scientists from government research institutions. This multidisciplinary structure allows graduate students to work across conventional disciplinary boundaries rather than being restricted to one narrow scientific field. The Toxicology Centre s broader mission is to train highly capable toxicologists who can contribute to emerging human and environmental health challenges while strengthening research, public engagement, technical outreach, and international leadership in toxicology. Degrees Available Applicants can pursue either a Master of Science or Doctor of Philosophy degree. Program Typical duration Format Delivery M.Sc. in Toxicology Approximately 2 years Research/thesis-based In person Ph.D. in Toxicology Approximately 3–4 years; USask lists 4 years as the expected length Research/dissertation-based In person The program is therefore designed primarily for students seeking advanced scientific research training rather than a classroom-only postgraduate qualification. Why Study Toxicology at the University of Saskatchewan? Toxicology sits at the intersection of environmental science, biology, chemistry, medicine, veterinary science, ecology, public health, and risk assessment. Students can investigate how pollutants and contaminants move through environmental systems, how living organisms respond to chemical exposure, how toxic substances affect human and animal health, and how scientific evidence can inform environmental regulation and risk management. USask highlights three broad strengths of its program: exposure to numerous areas of toxicology, interdisciplinary research involving university faculty and government scientists, and preparation for careers in government, consulting, industry, public health, and academia. The program has a particularly strong environmental and aquatic toxicology component, while faculty research spans a considerably broader spectrum. Toxicology Research Areas and Specializations Depending on supervisor availability and the applicant s research interests, potential areas of graduate specialization include: Analytical toxicology Aquatic toxicology Ecotoxicology Immunotoxicology Molecular and biochemical toxicology Nutritional toxicology Soil toxicology Environmental contaminant research Ecological and human-health risk assessment Veterinary toxicology Human toxicology Wildlife toxicology Forensic toxicology Radiation toxicology Molecular biology related to toxicological mechanisms Contaminant exposure and environmental chemistry The official University Catalogue confirms that the interdisciplinary program extends across areas such as analytical, aquatic, ecological, forensic, immunological, nutritional, radiation, veterinary, and wildlife toxicology. Examples of Research Available Through USask Toxicology The breadth of the faculty provides potential research opportunities involving topics such as heavy-metal neurotoxicity, exposure modelling, contaminant effects on aquatic organisms, livestock toxicology, environmental pollutants, computational chemistry, reproductive and developmental toxicology, food-web contamination, biomagnification, pesticides, northern ecosystems, metal bioaccumulation, selenium and human health, emerging contaminants, soil ecotoxicology, air pollution, cardiovascular effects, environmental genetics, DNA damage, and chemical mixtures. This interdisciplinary environment is particularly valuable for students whose research interests cross environmental, biological, chemical, veterinary, or human-health disciplines. Research Supervisors The University strongly recommends identifying and contacting a prospective supervisor before submitting an application. Applicants should review the faculty members associated with the Toxicology Graduate Program and identify researchers whose expertise aligns closely with their proposed area of study. Prospective students are encouraged to contact an appropriate faculty member with information about their academic background, research interests, and proposed graduate goals. If the faculty member is accepting new students and considers the applicant potentially suitable, the prospective supervisor may then advise the student to proceed with the formal application. Supervisor approval is described by the program as highly recommended before applying . This step should not be treated as a formality. For a research-based master s or Ph.D., the fit between the applicant s interests and the supervisor s active research program can be central to admission, research funding, and successful completion of the degree. Guaranteed Funding for Accepted Toxicology Graduate Students Funding is one of the strongest aspects of this opportunity. According to the official graduate-program page, all graduate students are guaranteed funding if accepted into the Toxicology program . The minimum stipend levels currently stated are: Degree Minimum stipend M.Sc. CAD 23,000 Ph.D. CAD 26,000 The Toxicology Centre further states that once a student has been accepted by a supervisor for their research program and has met the admission requirements, graduate students are guaranteed full funding. Basic health-insurance coverage is also identified as guaranteed by the Centre. Applicants should understand an important distinction: guaranteed funding does not mean that tuition and university fees disappear . Students are still assessed tuition and student fees. The stipend and other funding support should therefore be considered alongside the actual cost of enrollment. Additional Scholarships and Awards Graduate students may also have access to other University of Saskatchewan funding opportunities. Across the university, the College of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies administers more than CAD 14 million in scholarships annually , with funding originating from governments, university programs, donors, and individual academic units. The Toxicology Centre also lists program-specific awards and scholarships. These include opportunities such as an entrance scholarship for incoming M.Sc. and Ph.D. students, academic awards, research-presentation travel funding, and a Student Support Fund. Individual awards have their own eligibility criteria and deadlines and should not be confused with the standard guaranteed funding package attached to admission. M.Sc. in Toxicology Admission Requirements Applicants seeking admission to the master s program must generally hold a relevant undergraduate qualification. For the Toxicology M.Sc., USask requires a four-year honours degree or equivalent from a recognized university or college in an academic discipline relevant to the intended field of study , together with a minimum cumulative weighted average equivalent to 70% in the final two years of study . Proof of English-language proficiency may also be required. The Toxicology Centre provides additional academic guidance, indicating that applicants should normally have an undergraduate background in the life or natural sciences . Preparation in biology, chemistry, biochemistry, physiology, and statistics is particularly relevant, while previous study in environmental chemistry, ecology, pharmacology, or toxicology can be advantageous. Meeting the minimum academic threshold does not automatically guarantee admission. Ph.D. in Toxicology Admission Requirements Applicants seeking direct admission to the Ph.D. program normally require a master s degree or equivalent from a recognized institution in a discipline relevant to toxicology . The applicant must also generally have a cumulative weighted average of at least 70% on the USask grading-equivalent scale in the relevant master s coursework. English-language proficiency requirements may apply to international applicants and applicants whose first language is not English. As with the master s program, applicants should also demonstrate the capacity for independent academic research and advanced graduate study. M.Sc. Degree Requirements The M.Sc. is a research-based program. According to the 2026–2027 University Catalogue, students must maintain continuous registration in the required research course and complete relevant graduate ethics, seminar, research, and academic-course requirements. The program includes a minimum of nine credit units of core coursework , selected in consultation with the student s advisory committee and approved by the graduate chair. Additional ethics requirements apply where human or animal research is involved. The degree is therefore structured around both formal graduate study and substantial independent research. Ph.D. Degree Requirements The Ph.D. places greater emphasis on independent original research. Doctoral students must maintain continuous registration in their designated research course, complete required research and ethics components, participate in the toxicology seminar requirement, and complete at least six credit units selected in consultation with the advisory committee . Ph.D. candidates must also successfully complete a doctoral candidacy assessment and dissertation defense . English-Language Requirements for International Applicants Because instruction and examination at the University of Saskatchewan are conducted in English, applicants may be required to establish English proficiency. The university s current general graduate thresholds include the following: Test Minimum graduate-level requirement IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no component below 6.0 TOEFL iBT 86 overall with at least 19 in each area for the applicable scoring format; USask also publishes requirements for the revised TOEFL scale used for tests dated January 21, 2026 onward Cambridge C1 Advanced 176 overall Duolingo English Test 120 overall, with at least 100 in each area PTE Academic 63 overall, with at least 59 in each area CAEL 70 overall, with individual scores of at least 60 USask may also recognize qualifying previous study conducted entirely in English, subject to university and academic-unit rules. English tests generally remain valid for 24 months and must still be valid when the student begins the graduate program. Applicants should verify the current test requirements immediately before applying because language-testing systems and university thresholds can change. Tuition for M.Sc. Students in 2026–2027 The current posted tuition for thesis/project-based master s students is: 2026–2027 term Canadian students International students September–December CAD 1,902 CAD 4,279 January–April CAD 1,902 CAD 4,279 May–August CAD 1,902 CAD 4,279 Academic-year total CAD 5,706 CAD 12,837 These amounts do not include applicable student fees. Tuition for Ph.D. Students in 2026–2027 For doctoral students, domestic and international students currently pay the same published Ph.D. tuition rate: 2026–2027 term Tuition September–December CAD 1,879 January–April CAD 1,879 May–August CAD 1,879 Academic-year total CAD 5,637 This equal domestic/international Ph.D. tuition structure can be particularly significant for international doctoral applicants. Additional Student Fees Full-time on-campus students may also be assessed fees supporting services such as health and dental coverage, transit, and other student services. For the 2026–2027 academic year, the program page currently lists student fees of CAD 617.36 for Fall 2026, CAD 854.96 for Winter 2027, and CAD 46.75 each for Spring and Summer 2027 , subject to university policies and the student s enrollment circumstances. Applicants should therefore budget using both tuition and student fees rather than relying only on the tuition figure. Application Deadline There is no fixed application deadline . The University of Saskatchewan states that Toxicology applications are accepted on a year-round, continual basis . Students can begin the program in: January, May, or September. Because a research supervisor is highly recommended and international applicants may require significant time for study-permit processing, applying well ahead of the intended start term is prudent even though there is no formal program deadline. Application Process A prospective applicant should first investigate the available research areas and identify an appropriate Toxicology faculty member whose work aligns with their interests. After discussing potential supervision, the applicant can submit the formal University of Saskatchewan graduate application. The online application requests personal details, the applicant s complete post-secondary academic history, and information for three referees . Two referees must be academic contacts, while the third may be either academic or professional. The university estimates that the initial online application takes approximately 30 minutes and allows applicants to save their progress before submission. Application Fee The current non-refundable graduate application fee is: Canadian/domestic applicant: CAD 125 International applicant: CAD 145 The application will not proceed to processing until the required fee has been paid. Documents Applicants Should Prepare After submitting the online application and paying the fee, applicants receive access to the Supplemental Items Documents section of the application system. Applicants are initially required to upload unofficial PDF transcripts from each post-secondary institution they attended. Documents must include the institution s grading information or legend, and all pages of each transcript should be combined into one PDF. Transcripts issued in languages other than English need a certified English translation. Official transcripts are generally requested from applicants who receive an offer of admission. Depending on the applicant and program assessment, additional documentation can include a current CV or résumé , a statement or letter of intent describing experience and interest in toxicology , English-language test evidence where required, and letters of recommendation. What to Include in a Strong Statement of Intent For a research-based program of this nature, applicants should avoid sending a generic statement that simply says they are interested in science or environmental protection. A strong statement should clearly establish the applicant s academic preparation, previous research or laboratory exposure, proposed area of toxicology, methodological interests, reasons for choosing USask, and the connection between those interests and a potential supervisor. Applicants should also explain how their previous academic or professional experience prepares them for independent graduate research and what they hope to accomplish through the M.Sc. or Ph.D. International Students and Canadian Study Permits International students are explicitly considered within the University s graduate admission process. For current Canadian immigration procedures reflected on the USask website, master s and doctoral students applying for a Canadian study permit do not require a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) . USask advises international applicants to review current federal study-permit requirements before applying because immigration policies can change independently of university admission rules. Admission to the university and approval of a Canadian study permit remain separate processes. Indigenous and Under-Represented Applicants The Toxicology Graduate Program specifically states that it encourages applications from Indigenous students and individuals from under-represented groups . USask explains that incorporating diverse perspectives and knowledge systems can improve the relevance and impact of environmental and toxicological research. This is an encouragement and inclusion statement, however, rather than a restriction: the general Toxicology M.Sc. and Ph.D. programs are not limited to applicants from a particular racial or ethnic group. Career Opportunities After a Toxicology Graduate Degree The interdisciplinary nature of toxicology can prepare graduates for positions across environmental science, regulatory work, research, industry, health, and academia. USask specifically identifies potential employment pathways in government, environmental consulting, industry, public health, and academic research . The Toxicology Centre also states that its graduates are prepared for careers with government agencies, consulting organizations, industrial employers, universities, and further postgraduate research. Career possibilities can vary considerably depending on the student s research specialization, laboratory capabilities, quantitative skills, publications, professional network, and regulatory expertise. Key Program Information at a Glance Item Details University University of Saskatchewan Location Saskatchewan, Canada Field Toxicology Degrees M.Sc. and Ph.D. Study format Research-intensive, in person Expected M.Sc. length Approximately 2 years Expected Ph.D. length Approximately 4 years M.Sc. minimum funding CAD 23,000 Ph.D. minimum funding CAD 26,000 Funding Guaranteed for accepted Toxicology graduate students International applicants Eligible Application deadline No fixed deadline; applications accepted year-round Entry terms January, May, September Supervisor Approval/contact highly recommended before applying M.Sc. academic threshold At least 70% USask equivalent in final two years Ph.D. academic threshold Relevant master s degree and at least 70% USask equivalent Application fee CAD 125 domestic; CAD 145 international Important Funding Clarification Applicants should not interpret the phrase “guaranteed funding” as meaning that there are no costs associated with studying at USask. The Toxicology program provides a guaranteed minimum stipend for accepted students, while the university separately charges tuition and student fees. Prospective students should therefore calculate the net financial position after tuition, university fees, living costs, insurance arrangements, transportation, housing, and other expenses. This distinction is especially important for international M.Sc. students because the published international master s tuition is higher than the domestic master s rate. Conclusion The University of Saskatchewan Toxicology M.Sc. and Ph.D. programs offer a strong opportunity for students seeking advanced, interdisciplinary research training in environmental, human, wildlife, analytical, aquatic, molecular, veterinary, and ecological toxicology. The combination of guaranteed graduate funding, minimum stipends of CAD 23,000 for M.Sc. students and CAD 26,000 for Ph.D. students, year-round applications, multiple annual entry points, and eligibility for international students makes the program particularly noteworthy for prospective researchers seeking graduate study in Canada. Prospective applicants should begin by identifying an appropriate research supervisor, assessing whether their academic background aligns with the program, preparing a focused research-oriented statement of intent, and completing the formal USask graduate application. There is no fixed application deadline , but applicants should apply sufficiently early for their intended January, May, or September start date, particularly if international study-permit processing will be required. title: Global Health Emerging Scholars (GHES) Fellowship 2027–28: NIH-Supported Global Health Research Fellowship for U.S. and LMIC Scholars
summary: The Global Health Emerging Scholars (GHES) Fellowship 2027–28 is now accepting applications from emerging health researchers interested in advanced, mentored training in global health research. Supported by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) through the Fogarty International Center (FIC), the fellowship provides a 12-month research training experience designed to prepare the next generation of researchers and health professionals to address major and emerging global health challenges. The GHES Fellowship brings together a consortium of leading U.S. universities, including Yale University, Stanford University, the University of California, Berkeley, and the University of Arizona , together with partner institutions in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The program offers research training opportunities across 15 countries , providing fellows with the opportunity to work within international research environments while receiving mentorship from experienced global health researchers. For scholars seeking to develop a career in global health research, epidemiology, public health, medicine, disease prevention, health systems, environmental health, or related fields, the GHES Fellowship provides an opportunity to gain specialized research experience, strengthen academic and professional networks, and contribute to research addressing population health challenges. What Is the Global Health Emerging Scholars Fellowship? The Global Health Emerging Scholars (GHES) Fellowship is a 12-month, NIH-supported, mentored global health research training program. The fellowship is designed to improve population health by developing researchers who can conduct rigorous research and contribute to solutions for pressing health challenges around the world. The program is part of the Global Health Program for Fellows and Scholars/Launching Future Leaders in Global Health Research Training Program (LAUNCH) , which is sponsored by the Fogarty International Center and collaborating institutes and centers at the NIH . The fellowship year typically runs from July through June and provides participants with opportunities to undertake research training through a network of partner institutions in 15 LMICs. Rather than focusing solely on classroom-based education, the program emphasizes mentored research training . Fellows are connected with experienced faculty members and research institutions whose work aligns with their research interests. This structure allows participants to develop their research skills while gaining experience in international and multidisciplinary global health settings. GHES Fellowship 2027–28 Application Deadline The application for the 2027–28 GHES Fellowship year is currently open . Deadline: October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Applicants are encouraged to review the eligibility requirements carefully before submitting an application, particularly because eligibility requirements differ between U.S.-based applicants and applicants from LMICs. Who Is the GHES Fellowship Designed For? The fellowship is intended for emerging researchers at the predoctoral and postdoctoral levels. There are three major applicant categories: U.S. postdoctoral scholars U.S.-based doctoral or professional students Postdoctoral scholars based in eligible low- and middle-income countries The precise requirements depend on the applicant s academic status, citizenship or residency, institutional affiliation, and doctoral or professional qualifications. U.S. Postdoctoral Fellowship Eligibility U.S.-based postdoctoral applicants may be eligible if they meet the program s requirements. Applicants must generally: Be a U.S. citizen or U.S. resident . Provide a green card number where required for the application. Have completed a qualifying doctoral degree within the past five years or be on track to complete the doctoral degree by June 2027 . Obtain endorsement from appropriate GHES mentors. Have research interests that align with the expertise of available GHES mentors. Applicants may come from any U.S. academic institution , rather than being restricted exclusively to Yale University, Stanford University, UC Berkeley, or the University of Arizona. However, applicants who are not already affiliated with one of the consortium universities must obtain approval from the GHES Program Manager before applying. Such applicants are expected to provide information including: Their curriculum vitae. A description of their research interests. Potential GHES mentor(s) whose research aligns with their interests. An NIH biosketch where required. Information demonstrating that they have contacted potential mentors. The doctoral degrees considered for eligibility include, among others: PhD MD DVM DrPH PharmD Applicants should carefully confirm whether their specific degree and academic status meet the current eligibility requirements. U.S. Doctoral Student Fellowship Eligibility The GHES program also provides opportunities for eligible U.S.-based doctoral and professional students. Applicants in this category must generally: Be a U.S. citizen or U.S. resident . Be enrolled at UC Berkeley, the University of Arizona, Yale University, or Stanford University , or establish an appropriate affiliation with one of these institutions for the fellowship. Be advanced-candidacy doctoral students or eligible professional students. Professional students may include students pursuing degrees such as: MD DDS DVM PharmD Other qualifying professional degrees. Professional students must generally have completed at least three years of professional schooling. The program is therefore particularly relevant to advanced doctoral and professional students who are preparing to develop research careers in global health. LMIC Postdoctoral Fellowship Eligibility The GHES Fellowship also welcomes eligible postdoctoral scholars from low- and middle-income countries . For this category, applicants must generally: Be a citizen of a low- or middle-income country as defined by the World Bank . Have received a qualifying doctoral degree within the previous five years. Be affiliated with one of the GHES partner LMIC institutions. Obtain endorsement from appropriate GHES mentors. Have research interests that align with the available research training opportunities and mentors. Qualifying doctoral degrees can include: MBBS MMed PhD Other qualifying doctoral or professional degrees. Importantly, the LMIC postdoctoral category requires a doctoral or professional degree . A master s degree alone does not meet the stated requirement for this category. Countries and Regions Represented by the GHES Network The GHES consortium operates through collaborations involving institutions in 15 LMICs . The network spans multiple geographical regions, including: Africa Latin America The Caribbean South and Southeast Asia The Middle East Eastern Europe Oceania This international structure gives fellows access to research environments addressing health issues in different populations and geographic contexts. The program s partner-site model is particularly important because applicants are expected to identify research sites and mentors that align with their proposed research interests. Addis Ababa University mentors include: Dr. Miliard Derbew Dr. Tihitena Negussie Mammo Kenya The Stanford-associated site in Kenya is: Kenyatta National Hospital The Stanford University mentor is Christine Ngaruiya . Kenyatta National Hospital mentors include: Dr. Irene Inwani Dr. Cyrus Mugo Dr. John Kinuthia The Kenya site provides an important opportunity for eligible researchers whose interests align with the research conducted through the partner institution and available GHES mentors. Bangladesh The Stanford-associated Bangladesh site is: icddr;b Stanford University mentors include: Steve Luby Jade Benjamin-Chung The listed icddr;b mentors include: Rehnuma Haque Zhahirul Islam Mahbubur Rahman Rubhana Raqib Fahmida Tofail Senegal The Stanford-associated Senegal site is: Institut Pasteur de Dakar (IPD) The Stanford University mentor is Nathan Lo . The listed Institut Pasteur de Dakar mentors include: Daouda Ndiaye Amadou Sall Ines Vigan-Womas Uganda The Stanford-associated Uganda site is: Makerere University College of Health Sciences The Stanford University mentor is Prasanna Jaganathan . The listed Makerere University mentors include: Alfred Andama Richard Echodu Moses Kamya Achilles Katamba Martin Muddu Isaac Ssinabulya India The GHES network includes multiple research collaborations in India. One of the listed sites is: Christian Medical College Vellore (CMC) The Stanford University mentor is Jason Andrews , while Jacob John is listed as a Christian Medical College Vellore mentor. Another India-based collaboration is the: Kirk Smith Collaborative The Stanford University mentor is Andres Cardenas . The listed mentors associated with the Kirk Smith Collaborative include: Kalpana Balakrishnan Sagnik Dey Siuli Mukhopadhyay Naveen Puttaswamy Tavpritesh Sethi Chandra Venkataraman Why the GHES Fellowship Is Important for Global Health Researchers Global health challenges increasingly require researchers who can work across disciplines, institutions, countries and health systems. The GHES Fellowship is structured around this need by combining: Advanced research training International collaboration Faculty mentorship Institutional partnerships Population-health research Cross-country research experience Fellows have the opportunity to develop the skills necessary to contribute to evidence-based approaches to global health problems. The program also places participants within established research networks, allowing them to learn from researchers and institutions working directly on health challenges in diverse settings. What Applicants Should Consider Before Applying Prospective applicants should not treat the application as simply a general fellowship application. A strong understanding of the program s eligibility rules and research-site structure is essential. Before applying, applicants should consider the following: 1. Confirm your applicant category Determine whether you are applying as: A U.S. postdoctoral scholar A U.S. doctoral or professional student An LMIC postdoctoral scholar Each category has different requirements. 2. Verify your academic qualification Applicants should confirm that their degree meets the program s requirements. For LMIC postdoctoral applicants in particular, a master s degree alone is not sufficient according to the stated eligibility criteria. 3. Identify an appropriate research site Applicants should review the available GHES research sites and identify the location that best corresponds with their research interests. 4. Identify potential mentors Mentorship is central to the fellowship. Applicants should therefore investigate the research interests of available GHES faculty members and identify mentors whose expertise aligns closely with their proposed area of research. 5. Contact the appropriate program representative Applicants who are not already affiliated with one of the core consortium institutions may need to obtain eligibility confirmation from the GHES Program Manager before proceeding. Providing a CV, research-interest statement and information about the relevant research site and potential mentor can help the program determine whether the applicant is eligible. Application Process The GHES application is hosted through the Yale University Global Health Emerging Scholars program . Applicants should begin by carefully reviewing the program s eligibility and application information. For applicants seeking clarification, the Stanford GHES information recommends providing: A curriculum vitae. A short description of research interests. The research site and faculty member with whom the applicant s research interests are aligned. Any questions about eligibility or the application. Questions can be directed to Yosefa Gilon, GHES Stanford Program Manager , at the email address provided by the program. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours before the deadline to resolve questions about eligibility, institutional affiliation or potential mentorship. The opportunity is primarily intended for emerging global health researchers , including eligible U.S.-based doctoral/professional students, U.S. postdoctoral scholars and qualifying postdoctoral scholars from participating low- and middle-income countries. Applicants must satisfy the specific academic, citizenship/residency, institutional affiliation, degree and mentorship requirements applicable to their category. The program is therefore not a general scholarship open to all students worldwide . Eligibility is structured around specific academic and professional stages and, for LMIC applicants, participation in the GHES partner-site network. Visit HERE to learn more about the Global Health Emerging Scholars (GHES) Fellowship 2027–28. Race, Nationality and Geographic Eligibility The eligibility criteria provided do not specify a race or ethnic-group restriction . Geographic eligibility, however, is important. For the U.S. categories, applicants must generally be U.S. citizens or U.S. residents and meet the applicable academic and institutional requirements. For LMIC postdoctoral applicants, applicants must be citizens of a World Bank-defined low- or middle-income country , must have the required doctoral qualification, and must be affiliated with an eligible GHES partner institution. The program s research network covers 15 LMICs across several regions of the world. Applicants should therefore verify that their nationality and institutional affiliation satisfy the current GHES requirements before applying. Conclusion The Global Health Emerging Scholars (GHES) Fellowship 2027–28 offers a specialized 12-month pathway for emerging researchers who want to build careers in global health research. Supported by the NIH and delivered through a consortium involving Yale University, Stanford University, UC Berkeley and the University of Arizona , the program connects fellows with mentors and research institutions across an international network of 15 LMICs. The fellowship can be particularly valuable for researchers interested in developing advanced research capabilities while working on population-health challenges in international settings. Its emphasis on mentorship, institutional collaboration and research-site alignment makes choosing an appropriate research focus and mentor an important part of the application process. Eligible applicants should carefully review the requirements for their specific category, identify an appropriate GHES research site and mentor, and prepare the required application materials well before the deadline. The application deadline is October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. title: York University YSpace Venture Catalyst 2026: Free Startup Program for Early-Stage Technology Founders
summary: Applications are now open for the York University YSpace Venture Catalyst 2026 , a highly practical entrepreneurship program designed to help early-stage technology founders transform innovative ideas into stronger, validated, and potentially market-ready ventures. Delivered through YSpace, York University’s entrepreneurship and innovation hub , the Venture Catalyst program provides founders with structured business development support, expert mentorship, interactive workshops, peer-to-peer learning, and access to an entrepreneurial ecosystem designed to help startups avoid common early-stage mistakes and accelerate progress. For the current Fall 2026 cycle, applications officially opened on August 25, 2026 , and interested founders must submit their applications by September 25, 2026 . Successful applicants are expected to receive final acceptance decisions by October 9, 2026, with programming beginning on October 21, 2026 and concluding with Demo Day on December 10, 2026. One of the strongest features of the York University YSpace Venture Catalyst is that participation is free , and YSpace states that it does not take equity in participating companies . The program is also not restricted solely to York University students or alumni, making it accessible to eligible founders from the wider entrepreneurial community. About the York University YSpace Venture Catalyst Program The Venture Catalyst is an intensive early-stage startup development program that supports entrepreneurs who are still shaping their business concept, validating an idea, developing a proof-of-concept, or refining an early minimum viable product. The program is operated by YSpace at York University in partnership with the Black Entrepreneurship Alliance (BEA) . YSpace describes itself as York University’s pan-university entrepreneurship and innovation hub, supporting startups, scaleups, students, researchers, entrepreneurs, and founders from different sectors and communities. The Venture Catalyst is particularly relevant for technology entrepreneurs who have an innovative concept but need structured guidance to determine whether the concept has genuine commercial potential. Instead of focusing only on theoretical entrepreneurship education, Venture Catalyst is structured around practical venture development. Participants are expected to work directly on their companies, test assumptions, improve their business models, develop customer strategies, and make measurable progress toward launching or strengthening their products. The current program is described as a two-month program for early-stage founders, whether they are developing their first concept or already refining an MVP. What Is the Main Purpose of Venture Catalyst? Many promising technology startups fail during their earliest stages because founders begin developing products without adequately validating the customer problem, target market, value proposition, business model, or go-to-market strategy. The York University Venture Catalyst aims to address these challenges. During the program, entrepreneurs are supported in critically testing and improving different components of their ventures. The program is intended to help founders: Validate whether their startup idea addresses a meaningful market problem. Test important assumptions behind their business model. Better understand potential customers and users. Strengthen their value proposition. Develop practical customer development strategies. Improve their go-to-market strategy. Establish measurable venture development milestones. Refine or prepare an MVP. Generate early market traction. Learn from experienced entrepreneurs and industry professionals. Avoid potentially expensive mistakes during the early development stage. Prepare the venture for longer-term growth. According to YSpace, the program goes beyond simple idea validation. Founders are expected to stress-test their business models, sharpen their go-to-market strategies and strengthen early traction so their ventures are built on stronger foundations. Who Is Venture Catalyst Designed For? The Venture Catalyst is primarily intended for early-stage technology founders . The ideal applicant is not necessarily expected to operate an established or profitable business. In fact, the program specifically targets entrepreneurs who may still be working through the ideation and early validation stages. According to the official eligibility information, Venture Catalyst serves founders who are: Going through the ideation process. Validating the feasibility of their business concepts. Developing innovative technology-based ideas. Motivated to transform those ideas into viable ventures. Coachable and receptive to advice. Collaborative and willing to participate in the startup community. Demonstrating a growth mindset. Prepared to commit the necessary time to developing their venture. YSpace further explains that an ideal participating company is likely to still be in the ideation or early validation phase , with the objective of validating its target market and launching an MVP within approximately three months. Technology Startups Across Different Industries Can Apply A major advantage of Venture Catalyst is that the program is sector-agnostic within technology . This means applicants do not necessarily have to operate within one specific technology vertical. Technology-enabled businesses operating across different industries may potentially qualify, provided the venture meets the program s early-stage and innovation requirements. This could potentially include ventures operating in areas such as: Artificial intelligence Software and SaaS FinTech EdTech HealthTech Climate and sustainability technology Digital platforms E-commerce technology Enterprise software Consumer technology Data and analytics Smart infrastructure Mobility technology Transportation technology Electric vehicles Automation Internet of Things Other technology-enabled sectors Applicants should, however, demonstrate that technology forms a meaningful component of the business concept rather than merely being incidental to the venture. YSpace explicitly states that Venture Catalyst remains sector-agnostic and supports technology-based ventures operating across industries. Specialized Support for Black-Led Ventures The Venture Catalyst is delivered in partnership with the Black Entrepreneurship Alliance , or BEA. YSpace indicates that specialized support is available to Black-led businesses participating in the program. The Black Entrepreneurship Alliance is an initiative developed to strengthen entrepreneurship opportunities for Black founders through entrepreneurship education, mentorship, networking and business development support. YSpace s wider BEA programming has historically focused on helping Black entrepreneurs develop, launch, validate and scale their businesses. Importantly, the general Venture Catalyst program itself is not described on the current official application page as being restricted exclusively to Black founders . Specialized support is available for Black-led businesses, while the broader program welcomes qualifying early-stage technology entrepreneurs. Mobility Innovation Support Technology entrepreneurs working in mobility-related areas may also find the Venture Catalyst particularly relevant. YSpace has expanded its entrepreneurship ecosystem to support mobility ventures working on areas including: Transportation Electric vehicles Smart infrastructure Mobility technologies Automotive technologies Related technology solutions The main Venture Catalyst webpage states that the Winter cohort includes dedicated mobility innovation support through the Venture Mobility Catalyst. YSpace s broader SmartTO programming also supports innovation involving smart mobility, transportation, materials, energy systems, automotive technologies and related sectors. Founders specifically interested in the mobility stream should verify the availability of specialized mobility places for the relevant cohort when applying. What Participants Can Expect Successful applicants receive access to a structured venture development ecosystem rather than simply attending a series of lectures. The program combines several forms of support to help participating entrepreneurs systematically develop their companies. 1. Expert Mentorship Participants receive access to experienced mentors who can provide guidance on the strategic and operational challenges involved in developing an early-stage startup. Mentorship can be particularly valuable for founders who have strong technical ideas but limited experience commercializing products. 2. Hands-On Workshops Venture Catalyst includes workshops delivered with industry experts. These workshops are intended to provide founders with practical knowledge that can be immediately applied to their startups rather than remaining purely theoretical. 3. Peer-to-Peer Founder Sessions Entrepreneurship can be highly isolating, particularly during the ideation and validation stages. The Venture Catalyst incorporates peer-to-peer sessions that allow founders to learn from one another, share challenges, exchange experiences and build relationships within the startup ecosystem. 4. Office Hours with Subject-Matter Experts Participants can gain access to a private network of subject-matter experts through dedicated office hours. This can help founders obtain targeted advice relating to specific business challenges. 5. Dedicated Mentorship The program identifies a dedicated mentor as one of its key components, providing participants with additional guidance throughout their entrepreneurial journey. Leadership Development Venture Catalyst also places emphasis on strengthening founders themselves rather than focusing exclusively on the startup. Participants receive access to curated leadership content, personal-growth accountability and peer-to-peer support. This is significant because startup development frequently requires founders to develop new leadership competencies alongside their businesses. Entrepreneurs may need to learn how to communicate their vision, receive critical feedback, make difficult strategic decisions, manage uncertainty and eventually lead teams. The leadership-development element therefore complements the technical and commercial aspects of the program. Customer Development and Go-to-Market Strategy A core component of Venture Catalyst involves developing practical frameworks for bringing products to customers. Founders receive guidance related to customer development and go-to-market strategies. This can help entrepreneurs answer fundamental questions such as: Who is the ideal customer?
